title: Point-block recycling under budget pressure — regression evidence

defect.summary: Budget-driven eviction ignored the safe-eviction (anchor-resident) rule. reconcile() step 3 and the arrival-side evictToBudget() recycled a resident block whose nearest ancestor in the current cut was not resident yet (still in flight or backing off after a failure). The draw list then fell back to a coarser ancestor or nothing for that region: a coverage hole / coarse flicker under late uploads or fast view switches.
defect.rootCause: src/kernel/cache.ts evicted non-target residents purely by byte pressure; the anchor-resident check existed only in reconcile() step 2 (cut-transition eviction), not on the budget paths.
defect.fix: Unified evictToBudget() with the same anchor rule as the cut-transition path: candidates are non-target residents ordered LRU then deepest-first; a candidate whose cut anchor is not resident is deferred (counted as evictionsDeferred) instead of dropped. The cache may exceed its byte budget rather than tear a hole. The point budget itself is unchanged and still a hard cap in the selector.

minimalRepro.script: chain root(0) -> A(0/0) -> B(0/0/1); root+B resident (144264 bytes); A fails and backs off; byte budget shrunk to 72132 while B retires from the cut
minimalRepro.beforeFix: VIOLATION: B evicted while anchor A not resident -> region covered by root only (coarse hole)
minimalRepro.afterFix: no violation: B kept until A becomes resident; eviction deferred
minimalRepro.budgetsAreExplicit: all regression tests pass explicit tiny byte budgets (100/150/200 bytes); no default budget is relied on

identityAndMemoryPeak.method: window.scanStream.runTrajectory() headless (Chromium + WebGL2), same fixed camera path and budgets before and after the fix; per-waypoint drawn/resident/selected points are the point-identity proxy, peak resident bytes is the memory peak
